number_sense.title: Number Sense
number_sense.note: Number sense means choosing efficient ways to calculate and checking whether an answer makes sense.
number_sense.steps: Look for a friendly number; choose a strategy; calculate in small steps; estimate to check.
number_sense.mistakes: Rounding up but forgetting to subtract the extra.

whole_numbers.title: Whole Numbers
whole_numbers.note: Whole numbers are 0, 1, 2, 3 and so on. Place value determines the value of each digit.
whole_numbers.tips: Line up place values; estimate before calculating; use inverse operations to check.
whole_numbers.steps: Read the place value; choose the operation; calculate; check with estimation.
whole_numbers.mistakes: Misaligning digits or forgetting a carry.
whole_numbers.check: What is the value of the 7 in 47 305?

integers.title: Integers
integers.note: Integers include positive numbers, negative numbers and zero.
integers.tips: Same signs add magnitudes; different signs subtract magnitudes and keep the sign of the larger magnitude.
integers.steps: Identify signs; decide whether magnitudes add or subtract; attach the correct sign.
integers.mistakes: Treating a negative sign as an operation without considering the number's sign.

exponents.title: Exponents
exponents.note: An exponent tells how many times a base is used as a factor.
exponents.tips: Same base multiplication: add exponents. Same base division: subtract exponents. Power of a power: multiply exponents.
exponents.steps: Identify the base; identify the exponent rule; simplify; evaluate if required.
exponents.mistakes: Multiplying bases when bases are already the same.

patterns.title: Numeric Patterns
patterns.note: A pattern follows a rule. Look for the common difference or a multiplicative rule.
patterns.tips: Write term numbers; compare consecutive terms; test your rule on more than one term.
patterns.steps: Find the change; describe the rule; calculate the requested term; verify.

algebraic_expressions.title: Algebraic Expressions
algebraic_expressions.note: Variables represent numbers. Like terms have the same variable part.
algebraic_expressions.tips: Collect like terms; keep unlike terms separate; use brackets when substituting.
algebraic_expressions.steps: Identify like terms; combine coefficients; substitute carefully when values are given.
algebraic_expressions.mistakes: Combining unlike terms such as x and x².

algebraic_equations.title: Algebraic Equations
algebraic_equations.note: An equation states that two expressions are equal. Keep both sides balanced.
algebraic_equations.tips: Undo operations in reverse order; do the same operation to both sides.
algebraic_equations.steps: Simplify; isolate the variable; verify by substitution.
algebraic_equations.mistakes: Changing one side without changing the other.

geometry_lines.title: Geometry of Straight Lines
geometry_lines.note: Angles on a straight line add to 180° and angles around a point add to 360°.
geometry_lines.tips: Mark known angles; write the correct angle fact before calculating.
geometry_lines.steps: Identify the angle relationship; form an equation; solve; check the total.

pythagoras.title: Pythagoras
pythagoras.note: For a right-angled triangle, a² + b² = c² where c is the hypotenuse.
pythagoras.tips: The hypotenuse is opposite the right angle and is always the longest side.
pythagoras.steps: Identify c; substitute; calculate; take the square root if needed.
pythagoras.mistakes: Choosing the wrong side as c.
pythagoras.check: Find the hypotenuse when the legs are 6 and 8.

area_perimeter.title: Area & Perimeter
area_perimeter.note: Perimeter measures the distance around a shape. Area measures the surface inside it.
area_perimeter.tips: Perimeter uses linear units; area uses square units.
area_perimeter.steps: Identify the shape; choose the formula; substitute measurements; include units.
area_perimeter.example: Rectangle 8 cm by 5 cm: area = 40 cm²; perimeter = 26 cm.
area_perimeter.mistakes: Giving area in cm or perimeter in cm².
area_perimeter.check: Find the area of a 7 cm × 4 cm rectangle.

financial_maths.title: Financial Mathematics
financial_maths.note: Financial maths uses percentages, money, budgets, profit, loss, discounts and interest.
financial_maths.tips: Convert percentages to decimals; label money clearly; estimate before calculating.
financial_maths.steps: Identify the original amount; identify the percentage; calculate the change; state the final amount.
financial_maths.example: 20% of R500 = R100, so a 20% discount gives R400.
financial_maths.mistakes: Adding a discount when it should be subtracted.

transformations.title: Transformation Geometry
transformations.note: Translations move, reflections flip, rotations turn and enlargements change scale.
transformations.tips: Track a point before and after; use coordinates carefully.
transformations.steps: Name the transformation; identify the rule; apply it to every point; check orientation and size.
transformations.example: A translation 3 right and 2 up changes (x,y) to (x+3,y+2).
transformations.mistakes: Changing size during a translation or reflection.
transformations.check: What happens to (2,4) after translating 1 right and 3 down?

data_handling.title: Data Handling
data_handling.note: Data can be summarised with measures such as mean, median, mode and range.
data_handling.tips: Sort values before finding median; mean is total divided by number of values.
data_handling.steps: Organise data; choose the correct measure; calculate; interpret in context.
data_handling.mistakes: Using the middle value without sorting first.

probability.title: Probability
probability.note: Probability measures how likely an event is. It lies from 0 (impossible) to 1 (certain).
probability.tips: For equally likely outcomes, P(event)=favourable outcomes ÷ total outcomes.
probability.steps: Count favourable outcomes; count total outcomes; form and simplify the fraction.
probability.example: 2 red counters out of 5 gives P(red)=2/5.
probability.mistakes: Using total outcomes as the numerator.
probability.check: A fair die: what is P(rolling a 6)?
